content.title: About
content.content: Whiskey sour is a classic cocktail made with whiskey, fresh lemon juice, and simple syrup. Sometimes an egg white is added for a silky foam. The drink balances acidity, sweetness, and the woody notes of the whiskey.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded Whiskey sour recipe appeared in 1862 in "The Bartender's Guide".
It is one of the five "essential" cocktails (Old Fashioned, Martini, Manhattan, Daiquiri, Whiskey Sour) listed in the 1930s "Savoy Cocktail Book".
The original recipe called for American bourbon, though rye whiskey is also common today.
Egg white (the "float") is added to soften the acidity and create a smooth foam.
The drink’s popularity surged in the 2020s as craft bartenders experiment with fruit and spice variations.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Lemon juice is rich in vitamin C, which helps combat free radicals.

items.title: Moderate alcohol content
items.content: Moderate whiskey consumption may support cardiovascular health thanks to its polyphenols.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity of lemon stimulates gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake leads to health deterioration, dependence, and increased injury risk.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High amounts of lemon juice can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: If egg white is used, individuals with egg allergy may experience reactions.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Combine 45 ml bourbon, 30 ml fresh lemon juice, and 15 ml simple syrup in a shaker with ice. Optionally add 15 ml egg white. Shake vigorously for 10–12 seconds, then strain into a glass over fresh ice. Garnish with a maraschino cherry or a lemon wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ingredients separately: whiskey in a cool, dark place; lemons in the refrigerator; simple syrup in a sealed bottle in the fridge for up to a week. Use egg white immediately after separating.
